children: is making an unusually aggressive push into enterprise artificial intelligence, pitching its newest high-end Macs as an alternative to the expensive cloud infrastructure that has helped Nvidia
The argument is largely about economics.

Apple says businesses can run increasingly sophisticated AI workloads locally on Macs instead of continually paying cloud providers or AI developers for computing capacity measured in tokens. Its upgraded Mac mini and Mac Studio systems are aimed at tasks including software development and complex business workflows. Some configurations can approach $20,000.
Apple demonstrated just how far it wants to push that idea at its latest launch event.

The company connected four Mac Studios and used them to run a trillion-parameter AI model that identified and fixed a graphics coding problem, a workload that would ordinarily require data-center infrastructure. The four-machine setup operated from a single wall outlet.

Apple believes its unified-memory architecture and focus on power efficiency give Macs an advantage for running large models locally. The same architecture can also allow developers to move workloads across devices ranging from high-end Mac Studios to iPhones and iPads.
But Apple is attacking from far behind.

IDC estimates Macs hold only about 4.6% of the enterprise desktop market, compared with 91.3% for Microsoft Windows. Nvidia, meanwhile, remains dominant in data-center AI and is working with PC manufacturers to expand AI capabilities on Windows machines.

Apple does not need to replace Nvidia data centers or Windows PCs for this strategy to matter. The opportunity is to establish Macs as a credible middle ground between conventional corporate PCs and expensive cloud AI infrastructure. Investors should watch enterprise Mac adoption, demand for high-memory configurations, developer support and whether local inference becomes economically attractive enough to shift some workloads away from the cloud. Success could give Apple a larger role in enterprise AI while strengthening the Mac business beyond its traditional creative-user base.

title: Apple Takes AI Fight Straight to Nvidia and Microsoft
